Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National UGEL tried to stop me from inspecting UG hostels – Rent Commissioner Source : Albert Kuzor 18 November 2026 11:34am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku says the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) formally asked him not to inspect its hostel facilities through a letter written by the company's lawyers.
He said the letter was received ahead of his inspection of the university's hostels on Tuesday, which culminated in a heated confrontation between him and one of the hostel managers.
Speaking on Joy FM on Wednesday, November 18, Mr Opoku said UGEL, through its legal representatives, communicated its objection to his intended visit to the facilities.
"In fact, before we went there yesterday [Tuesday], they (UGEL) brought some lawyers, I don't know where they were coming from, and wrote a letter to me at the Rent Control that we shouldn't step there," he claimed.
The disclosure follows a viral video in which the Acting Rent Commissioner was seen in a heated exchange with a hostel manager during an inspection on the University of Ghana campus.
In the video, the manager is heard telling Mr Opoku that President John Dramani Mahama would not approve of his conduct.
The Commissioner, visibly agitated, responded by accusing the manager of stealing money and challenging him to take the matter to court.

The incident has generated public debate about the authority of the Rent Control Department to inspect hostel facilities and the responsibilities of property managers to comply with rent regulations.
The incident comes as the Acting Rent Commissioner intensifies nationwide inspections as part of efforts to enforce rent regulations and address concerns over the conduct of landlords and property managers.
